name: Syun Olav
subtitle: everyday mutton and potato curry in a thin, red, chilli-warm gravy

ingredients.qty: 600g, on the bone, cut into 4cm pieces

ingredients.note: small waxy potatoes left whole are better still

prepNotes: Halve the potatoes and keep them in cold water until you fry them, or they will grey in the time it takes to brown the meat.
Mix the Kashmiri chilli with 4 tbsp water to a loose paste before it goes in — dry powder scorches in mustard oil and turns brown instead of red.
Bring the mutton to room temperature for 20 minutes; straight from the fridge it seizes and takes longer to tenderise.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking point in a pressure cooker, then reduce the heat.
Fry the drained potato halves until golden on the cut sides, about 6 minutes, and lift them out.
steps.tip: Frying the potatoes first stops them disintegrating into the gravy later.

steps.text: Add the sliced onion and fry until deep gold, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring so the edges do not blacken.
steps.tip: Deep gold, not brown. Burnt onion turns the whole pot bitter.

steps.text: Stir in the garlic and ginger and fry 2 minutes.
Add the mutton with the black cardamom, cloves and cinnamon and brown over high heat for 8 minutes until the pieces have colour on every side.
Lower the heat, add the chilli paste, fennel powder, dry ginger powder, turmeric and salt and fry until the oil separates, about 6 minutes.
steps.tip: Wait for the oil to come to the surface as a red rim; that is the signal the masala is cooked.

steps.text: Pour in the hot water, close the cooker and cook for 4 whistles, then let the pressure fall on its own.
Open, add the fried potatoes and simmer uncovered for 12 minutes until they are tender to a knife tip and the gravy has thickened slightly.
Taste for salt, scatter over the garam masala and coriander leaves and take off the heat.
steps.tip: The gravy should stay pourable — this is a thin curry meant to be eaten over rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat on the stovetop with a splash of water; the potatoes soak up gravy overnight, so loosen it before serving.
